text:
When he comes, oh, I do not know
what I will wrap him in,
what.


Oh, tell me, moon,
when in your arms of enchantment
you take the sturdy oak
and rock him in your cradle.
Tell me, I do not know
what I will touch him with,
what.


Oh, tell me, breeze,
who with your kisses so light
stir the highest leaf,
comb the smoothest feather.
Tell me, and I will not say
what I will kiss him with,
what.


And now, as I remember,
Angel of the Lord, you,
tell me, for I received
your message: “behold the handmaid.”
Yes, tell me, by your faith,
what I will embrace him with,
what.


Or tell me, if not you,
if you know, Joseph,
and I will obey you,
for I am only a girl;
with what hands shall I hold him
so he will not break, oh,
with what.

translation.title: When He Comes, Oh, I Do Not Know...
translation.editorial_note:
Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.
